newsitem.title: USA: Feb cash flow to U.S. stock funds $18.45 bln - ICI.
newsitem.headline: Feb cash flow to U.S. stock funds $18.45 bln - ICI.

text.p: U.S. stock mutual funds received net new cash inflows of $18.45 billion in February, the Investment Company Institute said Thursday.
That was down from an estimate of $19.5 billion for the month issued March 13 and well off the record $29.08 billion that flowed into stock funds in January.
For the first two month of 1997, flows to stock funds were $47.53 billion, a little lower than the $51.28 billion for the corrresponding period in 1996, the trade group said.

ICI said bond and income funds had inflows of $2.17 billion in February compared with $3.40 billion in January. Year-to-date flows for these funds of $5.57 billion compare with $6.22 billion in the same period of 1996.
Money market funds had an inflow of $21.10 billion in February compared with $21.18 billion in January.
Net new cash flow into the entire mutual fund industry was $41.72 billion in February, compared with $53.66 billion in the previous month.
ICI deputy chief economist Mitchell Post said the decline in February's inflow from January's record level partly relected a seasonal pattern.
"January typically receives the largest seasonal inflows, which reflect, among other things, retirement account activity and the investment of year-end bonuses," Post said in a statement.
